records.gloss: For the director, for Jeduthun. A psalm of David.
pieces: For the music director. For Jeduthun. A psalm of David.

L.1: For the director: for Jeduthun. A psalm of David.

R.1: For the leader of the music. For Jeduthun. A song of David.

decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.
As in 4:1.

decisions.choice: Jeduthun: a leader of the temple singers
decisions.reason: Jeduthun was one of the leaders of the music at the sanctuary in David's time (1 Chronicles 16:41; 25:1). His name also stands in the titles of Psalms 62 and 77.

decisions.choice: Jeduthun: the name as read, not as written
decisions.reason: The Hebrew writes the name with a slightly different spelling and its notes say to read it as Jeduthun. The words follow the form to be read.

records.heading: My life is only a breath

records.source: אָמַ֗רְתִּי אֶֽשְׁמְרָ֣ה דְרָכַי֮ מֵחֲט֪וֹא בִלְשׁ֫וֹנִ֥י אֶשְׁמְרָ֥ה לְפִ֥י מַחְס֑וֹם בְּעֹ֖ד רָשָׁ֣ע לְנֶגְדִּֽי׃
records.gloss: I said, I will guard my ways from sinning with my tongue; I will keep for my mouth a muzzle while [the] wicked [is] before me.
pieces: I made up my mind: "I will be careful how I live, so that my tongue does not lead me into sin. I will keep my mouth muzzled for as long as the wicked stand before me."

L.2: I said, "I will guard my ways from sinning with my tongue; I will keep a muzzle on my mouth while [the] wicked [is] in front of me."

R.2: I decided, "I will be careful not to sin by what I say. I will keep my mouth shut while wicked people are around me."

decisions.reason: Here "I said" is a resolve made within, as often in the Psalms (30:7).
The word (machsom) occurs only here; it is a muzzle such as is put on an animal.

decisions.choice: while the wicked is before me: why he keeps silent
decisions.reason: He holds back his complaint while the wicked can hear it, so as not to sin by speaking against God in front of them.

The Hebrew describes "the wicked" as one person ("he", "his") who stands for all who act this way. Balanced and Readable make the portrait plural, which is how "the wicked" is heard in English and includes men and women alike; Literal keeps the Hebrew singular.

records.source: נֶאֱלַ֣מְתִּי ד֭וּמִיָּה הֶחֱשֵׁ֣יתִי מִטּ֑וֹב וּכְאֵבִ֥י נֶעְכָּֽר׃
records.gloss: I was mute [with] silence; I held still from good, and my pain was stirred up.
pieces: I said nothing at all; I held my peace, even from saying good, and my pain grew sharper.

L.3: I was mute in silence; I kept quiet [even] from good, and my pain was stirred up.

R.3: So I kept completely quiet. I would not even speak good words. But that only made my pain worse.

decisions.choice: kept quiet from good: even from good words
alternatives: to no avail (it did no good)
decisions.reason: The phrase is short: "I kept silent from good". It may mean he held back even good words, or that his silence did no good.
The verb ('akar) is to stir up or trouble; holding in his grief made it worse.
Readable makes the link between the silence and the pain plain, as the meaning decision reads it (m2).

records.gloss: My heart grew hot within me; in my sighing a fire burned; I spoke with my tongue.
pieces: Inside me my heart was burning; as I brooded, it flared into fire, and at last I spoke:

L.4: My heart grew hot within me; in my musing a fire burned; I spoke with my tongue:

R.4: I felt hot inside, as if a fire were burning. The more I thought about it, the worse it got. Finally I spoke up.

decisions.reason: The word (hagig) is rare: a murmuring or sighing, inward thought that is almost spoken (Psalm 5:2).

decisions.choice: my heart grew hot, a fire burned: feeling that could not be held in
decisions.reason: Held-in grief is pictured as a fire that must break out, as with Jeremiah (Jeremiah 20:9).
The sentence leads into the words he spoke, which are the prayer of verses 5-14; a colon shows that, without quotation marks around the whole prayer.

records.source: הוֹדִ֘יעֵ֤נִי יְהוָ֨ה׀קִצִּ֗י וּמִדַּ֣ת יָמַ֣י מַה־הִ֑יא אֵ֝דְעָ֗ה מֶה־חָדֵ֥ל אָֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Make known to me, YHWH, my end and the measure of my days, what it [is]; let me know how fleeting I [am].
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, let me know my end and how many days are measured out for me; let me understand how short-lived I am.

L.5: Make known to me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, my end, and the measure of my days, what it [is]; let me know how fleeting I [am].

R.5: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, show me when my life will end. Show me how many days I have. Help me understand how short my life is.

decisions.choice: my end, the measure of my days: to grasp how brief life is
alternatives: to learn the date of his death
decisions.reason: The prayer is not for a date but for a true sense of how short life is (Psalm 90:12).
The word (chadel) describes what stops or comes to an end.

records.source: הִנֵּ֤ה טְפָח֨וֹת׀נָ֘תַ֤תָּה יָמַ֗י וְחֶלְדִּ֣י כְאַ֣יִן נֶגְדֶּ֑ךָ אַ֥ךְ כָּֽל־הֶ֥בֶל כָּל־אָ֝דָ֗ם נִצָּ֥ב סֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: Look, handbreadths you have made my days, and my lifespan [is] like nothing before you; surely all vanity [is] every human standing. Selah.
pieces: See, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made my days only a few hand widths long; my whole lifetime is as nothing in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sight. Every human being, however firmly they stand, is only a breath. Selah

L.6: Look, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made my days handbreadths, and my lifetime [is] as nothing before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; surely every human, [though] standing firm, [is] all breath. Selah

R.6: You have made my life very short, only as wide as a hand. My whole life is nothing compared to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Every person is like a breath of air. Selah

decisions.reason: A handbreadth (tefach) is the width of four fingers, one of the smallest measures in daily use (Exodus 25:25).

decisions.choice: breath: vapor, what passes at once
decisions.reason: The word (hevel) is a breath or vapor, the word of Ecclesiastes 1:2. It returns in verses 7 and 12.
The word (nitsav) means standing firm; even a person who seems secure is only breath.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.
Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

records.source: אַךְ־בְּצֶ֤לֶם׀יִֽתְהַלֶּךְ־אִ֗ישׁ אַךְ־הֶ֥בֶל יֶהֱמָי֑וּן יִ֝צְבֹּ֗ר וְֽלֹא־יֵדַ֥ע מִי־אֹסְפָֽם׃
records.gloss: Surely as a shadow a man walks about; surely [in] vain they are in turmoil; he heaps up and does not know who will gather them.
pieces: Truly, people go about like shadows; their busy noise is all for nothing; they pile things up, not knowing who will collect them.

L.7: Surely as a shadow {{gender:a person|a man}} walks about; surely for nothing they bustle about; {{gender:they heap|he heaps}} up [wealth] and {{gender:do|does}} not know who will gather it.

R.7: People are like shadows moving around. They rush around for nothing. They store up riches, but they do not know who will get them.

decisions.choice: a shadow: an image without substance
decisions.reason: The word (tselem) is an image or likeness; here it is a mere outline, like a shadow (Psalm 73:20).

decisions.choice: heaps up: wealth, though the object is not named
decisions.reason: The verb (tsavar) is to pile up, used of grain and silver (Genesis 41:35; Job 27:16); others will gather what he has stored (Luke 12:20).

decisions.choice: inclusive wording by default; the traditional "he" or "man" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses a masculine singular for a person who stands for anyone of this kind, so the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default and the traditional form as the alternative.
The Hebrew word is masculine but stands for anyone who lives this way. Balanced and Readable speak of people in general, which needs no setting; Literal keeps the singular with the gender setting.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֣ה מַה־קִּוִּ֣יתִי אֲדֹנָ֑י תּ֝וֹחַלְתִּ֗י לְךָ֣ הִֽיא׃
records.gloss: And now what do I wait for, Lord? My hope, it [is] in you.
pieces: So then, Lord, what is left for me to wait for? My hope rests on {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.8: And now, what do I wait for, Lord? My hope, it [is] in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.8: So, Lord, what can I look forward to? I put my hope in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: And now: the turn of the psalm
decisions.reason: From the shortness of life the psalmist turns to God: if life is a breath, hope can rest only in him.
As in 38:10.

records.gloss: From all my transgressions deliver me; [the] reproach of [the] fool do not make me.
pieces: Rescue me from all my rebellious acts; do not make me something fools laugh at.

L.9: From all my transgressions deliver me; do not make me the reproach of [the] fool.

R.9: Save me from all the wrong things I have done. Do not let foolish people make fun of me.

decisions.choice: the fool: one who scorns God
decisions.reason: The fool (naval) in the Psalms is not slow-witted but one who lives as if there were no God (Psalm 14:1).
The word (pesha') is rebellion, a breach of loyalty.

records.source: נֶ֭אֱלַמְתִּי לֹ֣א אֶפְתַּח־פִּ֑י כִּ֖י אַתָּ֣ה עָשִֽׂיתָ׃
records.gloss: I am mute; I do not open my mouth, for you have done [it].
pieces: I stay silent and say nothing, because this is {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} doing.

L.10: I am mute; I do not open my mouth, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done [it].

R.10: I am quiet. I do not say anything, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the one who did this.

decisions.choice: you have done it: the suffering is from God's hand
decisions.reason: His silence now is different from verse 3: he accepts that his suffering comes from God, and speaks only to God.

records.source: הָסֵ֣ר מֵעָלַ֣י נִגְעֶ֑ךָ מִתִּגְרַ֥ת יָ֝דְךָ֗ אֲנִ֣י כָלִֽיתִי׃
records.gloss: Remove from upon me your stroke; from the hostility of your hand I am finished.
pieces: Take {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} blow away from me; I am worn out by the force of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand.

L.11: Remove {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} blow from upon me; by the hostility of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand I am worn out.

R.11: Please stop punishing me. The force of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand has worn me out.

decisions.reason: As in 38:12.
The word (tigrah) occurs only here; it comes from a verb meaning to stir up strife.

records.source: בְּֽתוֹכָ֘ח֤וֹת עַל־עָוֺ֨ן׀יִסַּ֬רְתָּ אִ֗ישׁ וַתֶּ֣מֶס כָּעָ֣שׁ חֲמוּד֑וֹ אַ֤ךְ הֶ֖בֶל כָּל־אָדָ֣ם סֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: With rebukes for iniquity you discipline a man, and you melt like the moth his treasure; surely vanity [is] all humankind. Selah.
pieces: You punish people for their wrongs with rebukes, and like a moth {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} eat away what they love most. Every human being is only a breath. Selah

L.12: With rebukes for iniquity {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} discipline {{gender:a person|a man}}, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} consume like the moth what {{gender:they hold|he holds}} dear; surely every human [is] a breath. Selah

R.12: When {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} correct people for their sin, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} destroy what they love, the way a moth eats cloth. Every person is like a breath of air. Selah

decisions.choice: like the moth: slow, quiet destruction
decisions.reason: The moth eats cloth little by little until it falls apart (Job 13:28; Isaiah 50:9).

decisions.choice: what he holds dear: beauty, wealth, all that is desired
decisions.reason: The word (chamud) is what is desired or treasured.
As in verse 6, the refrain returns.

decisions.choice: inclusive wording by default; the traditional "he" or "man" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses a masculine singular for a person who stands for anyone of this kind, so the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default and the traditional form as the alternative.
The Hebrew word is masculine but stands for anyone who lives this way. Balanced and Readable speak of people in general, which needs no setting; Literal keeps the singular with the gender setting.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.
Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

records.source: שִֽׁמְעָ֥ה־תְפִלָּתִ֨י׀יְהוָ֡ה וְשַׁוְעָתִ֨י׀הַאֲזִינָה֮ אֶֽל־דִּמְעָתִ֗י אַֽל־תֶּ֫חֱרַ֥שׁ כִּ֤י גֵ֣ר אָנֹכִ֣י עִמָּ֑ךְ תּ֝וֹשָׁ֗ב כְּכָל־אֲבוֹתָֽי׃
records.gloss: Hear my prayer, YHWH, and my cry for help give ear to; at my tears do not be silent, for a sojourner I [am] with you, a resident alien like all my fathers.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, hear what I pray; turn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ear to my plea for help, and do not keep silent when I weep. I am only a guest with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, a foreigner passing through, just like my ancestors before me.

L.13: Hear my prayer, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and give ear to my cry for help; at my tears do not be silent, for I [am] a sojourner with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, a resident alien like all my fathers.

R.13: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, listen to my prayer! Hear me when I cry for help. Do not ignore my tears. I am only staying with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for a short time, like a visitor, the way my ancestors were.

decisions.choice: sojourner, resident alien: a guest on another's land
decisions.reason: A sojourner (ger) and a resident alien (toshav) lived on land that belonged to someone else, with no rights of their own. The land is the LORD's, and his people live on it as his guests (Leviticus 25:23; 1 Chronicles 29:15).

decisions.choice: do not be silent: do not refuse to answer
decisions.reason: God's silence is his not answering (Psalm 28:1).

records.source: הָשַׁ֣ע מִמֶּ֣נִּי וְאַבְלִ֑יגָה בְּטֶ֖רֶם אֵלֵ֣ךְ וְאֵינֶֽנִּי׃
records.gloss: Look away from me, that I may brighten up, before I go and am no more.
pieces: Turn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} gaze from me, and let me find joy again before I leave and am no longer here.

L.14: Look away from me, that I may brighten [again], before I go and am no more.

R.14: Stop looking at me in anger. Let me be happy again before I die and am gone.

decisions.choice: look away: turn your searching gaze from me
decisions.reason: The verb (sha'ah, in this form) is to look away; the form may also come from a verb meaning to smear or shut the eyes (Isaiah 6:10). Either way the psalmist asks God to stop watching him in judgment (Job 7:19; 14:6).
The verb (balag) is to brighten up (Job 9:27; 10:20).

decisions.choice: before I go and am no more: the psalm ends in the shadow of death
decisions.reason: Like Psalm 88, the psalm ends without a word of answer; the prayer itself is an act of trust.
Readable says what kind of looking the psalmist asks God to stop (m1).
